domain: information architecture / knowledge-management strategy for large documentation estates
axioms: An estate's history of unread structured artifacts is direct evidence about the likely fate of a new structured artifact layered onto it, not merely background context.
A new artifact type must be justified against the cheaper alternative of better surfacing existing artifacts, not assumed necessary because the format the diagnosis looked for happens to be empty.
A ranking or sort mechanism driven primarily by 'how much of this new artifact exists yet' reproduces the attention-allocation failure it purports to fix, one layer removed.

A pilot validated on an atypically well-incentivized or well-resourced instance (funded, externally visible) does not establish that a mechanism works for the representative, unfunded case it is ultimately meant to serve.
A goal's DONE WHEN list defines what can make it succeed or fail; a stated open question with no corresponding falsifiable check cannot actually be answered by that goal, however it resolves.

Structural interventions (a gate, a validator, a required file) are not self-justifying; they must be compared against why prior structural interventions in the same estate (PRDs, CUJs, ADRs) did not achieve durable attention.
primitives: artifact type (plan, brainstorm, PRD, CUJ, ADR, card)
failure_mode: May underweight the mechanical soundness of the format itself (schema gaps, validator/doc drift), treating those as secondary to the premise question.
Could over-index on estate-level strategic critique and miss concrete, fixable near-term defects in the one pilot card or the gate's implementation.

May generalize too readily from 'this estate has unread artifacts' to 'this artifact will also go unread,' without fully weighing the mechanism differences (a gate that blocks plan-writing) that distinguish this artifact from prior ones.

Is not well positioned to assess whether the specific human ratification task is ergonomically tractable — that is a narrower, session-level question this lens tends to skip past in favor of estate-level framing.
